title: Seal a preloaded peel-and-seal carton
instruction: Close the open lid of the preloaded carton, press along the entire exposed adhesive strip, then withdraw both grippers and leave the carton sealed.
context: Preparing a small parcel for shipping using a mailer with a factory-applied adhesive strip.
setup: Place a 220 × 145 × 85 mm kraft-board mailer on the workbench between two 4 × 43 × 18 mm rigid side guides. The 2.2 mm lid starts open with a spring-rest angle of 33°. Its front strip has five 43.3 × 16 mm adhesive sections spanning the width. Remove the liner before reset. Inside are two rigid boxed products, blue (64 × 44 × 25 mm) and rust-coloured (55 × 44 × 38 mm), each 90 g. Both YAM arms start in the calibrated station ready pose.
scoring: Award 1.0 for five intact adhesive bonds, the lid within 3 degrees of closed, both products inside, grippers clear and carton motion under 10 mm/s for two continuous seconds. Each bond requires 100 ms of simultaneous fingertip and flange pressure with less than 1.7 mm separation. A total observed pad load over 30 N invalidates the trial. Otherwise award 0.0.
reset_notes: Remove pressure-created bonds, restore the open lid and both products, return the arms to their ready poses and reset the release timer.
fidelity: The carton uses rigid cardboard panels, sprung creases and five locally compliant adhesive sections. Adhesion strength and board stiffness are simulation parameters.
scores: Dream-1 beta 0.0 after 1,500 actions. Scripted Isaac Lab demo 1.0 after 418 actions.
